question: Did any BASS-II or FLEX test reach the lunar habitat oxygen level (30% or more)?
claim: None of the 129 BASS-II solid-fuel tests reached 30% oxygen (highest 22.2%), while 24 of the 274 FLEX droplet tests did, up to 34%.
summary_student: Solid materials such as plastics and fabrics were never burned in space at the oxygen level planned for a Moon base. Only some liquid fuel droplet tests reached that level.
summary_professional: BASS-II (PSI-25) initial O2 ranged 13.6–22.2% by volume over 129 tests, none at or above 30%. FLEX (PSI-69) initial O2 ranged 12–34% mole fraction over 274 droplet tests, 24 of them at or above 30%.

method.formula: For each investigation, the lowest and highest oxygen percentage over its tests that report oxygen, the number of those tests, and how many reached at least threshold_pct (o2_pct_max >= threshold_pct).

columns: O initial ambient composition; mole fraction

assumptions: Uses the initial oxygen level of each test.
Mole fraction and volume fraction are treated as equal (ideal gas).
limitations: Covers only BASS-II and FLEX, not every solid-fuel investigation in PSI.
No test at 30% oxygen means no data, not that these materials are safe or unsafe at that level.
Oxygen is compared alone; the lunar habitat also has a lower pressure, which this calculation does not compare.
warnings: PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data. Lunar and Mars conclusions are bounded by microgravity and Earth-gravity results only.

chart.idea: Range bars of the oxygen levels tested by BASS-II and FLEX, with a dashed line at the 30% lunar habitat target.

visual_offer.footnote: Want a visual? I can draw a chart comparing the oxygen levels tested by BASS-II and FLEX against the 30% lunar habitat target.
